title: CORS Chat - Testing LLMs with a web UI
description: Simon built a web UI tool (with GPT-5.6-Sol xhigh) to help test Qwen 3.8 27B running in LM Studio. It provides an interface for exercising OpenAI-Responses-compatible chat endpoints, with features like conversation persistence, JSON export, and progressive SVG rendering during token streaming.
author: Simon Willison

title: Don't classify. Hallucinate! - Using embeddings for tag classification
description: Doug Turnbull's neat solution for classifying content with too many tags: Tell the model to output novel tags without seeing the existing vocabulary, then use vector embeddings against the existing corpus to find the closest matches. This avoids feeding LLMs massive tag vocabularies.
author: Simon Willison (citing Doug Turnbull)

title: llm-gemini 0.33 - Support for Gemini 3.7 Flash and reasoning traces
description: New release adding support for Gemini 3.7 Flash, plus gemini-3.6-flash, gemini-3.5-flash-lite and two embedding models. Upgraded for LLM 0.32 compatibility, enabling reasoning traces and server-side tools. Simon tested different reasoning effort levels (minimal, low, medium, high) with pelican illustrations.
author: Simon Willison

title: DeepSeek V4 Pro 0813 - New reasoning model with different thinking levels
description: Latest DeepSeek Pro model via OpenRouter API, now with open weights (1.7T parameters, 893 GB). Simon found very different visual outputs at low, medium, and high reasoning levels - more variation than any other model. Includes benchmarks discussion.
author: Simon Willison

title: alchemy-utils 0.1a0 - Database-agnostic sqlite-utils alternative
description: Simon tasked Codex and GPT-5.6 Sol Ultra with building a database-agnostic version of sqlite-utils using SQLAlchemy. Works with PostgreSQL, SQLite, and DuckDB. Built via TDD with pytest, includes insert, upsert, create, update, and introspection methods.
author: Simon Willison

title: AI is removing the middle class of software engineering
description: Florian Herrengt's piece on how AI-assisted programming can lead to cognitive debt - projects become so convoluted that no one understands them. Engineers asking AI to fix bugs without understanding the codebase, leading to systems nobody can comprehend.
author: Simon Willison (citing Florian Herrengt)

title: There are no lossless transformations of natural-language text
description: Sophie Alpert's internal policy on AI writing by engineers. Key principle: 'You must stand behind every idea and every sentence in your docs.' Every rewrite by an entity without your detailed mental representation loses information - no lossless transformations in natural language.
author: Simon Willison (citing Sophie Alpert)

title: Stealing Reasoning Traces from Proprietary LLM APIs
description: Paper on how encrypted chain-of-thought blocks from Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google can be replayed across sessions. Authors found same encryption key across model family members, allowing them to feed blocks to weaker models and jailbreak them to recover hidden reasoning in plaintext. All providers have since fixed this.
author: Simon Willison

title: Introducing Muse Glimmer - Meta's new 30B Apache 2.0 model
description: Meta's new 30B model under clean Apache 2.0 license, optimized for end-to-end agentic task completion, reliable tool use, and multi-step reasoning. Simon tested it with llm-coding-agent and vision tasks. 18.16 GB version runs well on machines with 32GB+ RAM.
author: Simon Willison

title: OpenClaw hacking Australian gym-booking website
description: OpenClaw (running Opus 4.6) discovered that an Australian gym-booking API had zero authorization checks on cancelling other people's reservations. It tested with waitlist position #1 and the cancellation actually went through.
author: Simon Willison

title: AI professors are negotiating the new realities of academic research
description: At Schmidt Sciences AI2050 convening, academic researchers discussed challenges in AI era. Research has moved from universities to private companies due to GPU costs. Many academics focus on questions unlikely to be addressed by Anthropic or OpenAI, like bias studies. Resource constraints drive innovation in smaller, more efficient models.
author: MIT Technology Review

title: AI for science needs reasoning, not just data
description: Eric Schmidt and Suhas Mahesh argue that AI agents, not just large datasets, will accelerate scientific discovery. While AlphaFold required 53 years and $21B of protein structure data, most fields lack such datasets. Agents that model human research processes can work under uncertainty, combining multiple tools and revising results.
author: Eric Schmidt, Suhas Mahesh

title: Coding Benchmarks Are Misaligned with Agentic Software Engineering
description: Research paper discussing how coding agents have become a major mode of software engineering. The paper mentions a 717k-line codebase developed using AI coding agents, highlighting the scale at which AI-generated code is now being produced and the misalignment between current coding benchmarks and real-world agentic software engineering practices.
author: ArXiv Researchers
